item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-3224d3d92f917d2a","start_unit":14,"end_unit":15,"fact_summary":"Human Rights Watch reported increasing attacks against political opposition members ahead of the 2023 parliamentary elections; authorities allegedly arrested critics under the Digital Security Act, used approximately 20,000 opposition-related cases for raids and intimidation, targeted dissidents and their relatives, and harassed the human-rights organization Odhikar. HRW also reported that the government rejected allegations underlying 2021 sanctions against Rapid Action Battalion rather than pursuing reform.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.5","3B.8","4B.2","4B.3","4B.6","4B.9","7B.2","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report was published in January 2023 and describes conditions leading into the 2023 election, with some cited developments occurring in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the conduct to Bangladesh authorities and the ruling Awami League government during Sheikh Hasina's premiership; it does not establish her personal involvement in each act.","limitations":["The source is an external human-rights assessment and reports allegations and opposition claims alongside its own characterization; the supplied extract does not provide judicial findings or Hasina's response beyond the government's dismissal of sanctions-related allegations."]},{"source_id":"SRC-3224d3d92f917d2a","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"In Rohingya refugee settings, HRW reported that Bangladeshi authorities closed community-led schools, destroyed shops, restricted movement, and that refugees reported threats, extortion, arbitrary arrests, and torture by security forces. Authorities allowed humanitarian groups to teach the Myanmar curriculum but denied refugee children accredited education; about 8,000 refugees were moved to Bhasan Char in 2022, where HRW reported severe movement restrictions, shortages, and abuses, and prevention of return to the mainland.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.8","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report covers the situation entering 2023 and includes developments during 2022 that remained relevant during the target period.","ruler_attribution":"The report attributes the policies and alleged abuses to Bangladeshi authorities and security forces under the Hasina government; personal direction by Hasina is not shown in the extract.","limitations":["The supplied extract does not provide complete official statistics, adjudicated findings, or a comparison with inherited conditions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c3a61e67ddbe64a8","start_unit":1,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"Bangladesh submitted a national report for the Universal Periodic Review in 2023, dated 1 September 2023, to the UN Human Rights Council framework; the submission is identified as A/HRC/WG.6/44/BGD/1 and is 22 pages.","question_ids":["2B.6","3B.4","4B.4","5B.7","6B.5","7B.6","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Directly dated 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The document is a formal national submission by Bangladesh during Sheikh Hasina's premiership; the supplied metadata does not establish which claims or policies she personally authored.","limitations":["Only catalog metadata and no substantive report text are supplied, so the submission's claims, omissions, and implementation evidence cannot be assessed."]},{"source_id":"SRC-a84b63518e581e2e","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"UNHCR's 2023 Joint Response Plan for the Rohingya humanitarian crisis covered January through December 2023 and identified Bangladesh locations including Kutupalong, Nayapara, and Bhasan Char; it was published on 30 January 2024.","question_ids":["3B.7","3B.9","6B.2","6B.3","6B.6","6B.9","8B.1","8B.2","8B.5","8B.6"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"The plan concerns the full 2023 period, although publication occurred in January 2024.","ruler_attribution":"The document concerns humanitarian coordination in Bangladesh but the supplied extract does not attribute particular decisions to Hasina.","limitations":["The supplied extract contains no needs assessment, targets, funding execution, outcomes, or government-performance findings."]},{"source_id":"SRC-ad63468fd4fee2fa","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"WHO reported that Bangladesh's dengue upsurge began around the last week of April 2023, earlier than in previous years; by 27 August, 119,133 cases and 569 deaths had been reported across all 64 districts, creating additional pressure on the health system. WHO stated it was supporting national authorities in a coordinated response.","question_ids":["3B.6","3B.9","6B.2","6B.5","6B.6","6B.10","8B.5","8B.6","8B.7","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Situation report dated 4 September 2023 and reporting data through 27 August 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The report identifies national authorities as response counterparts but does not specify Hasina's personal decisions, resources, or responsibility.","limitations":["The extract reports outbreak scale and WHO support but does not evaluate the government's response quality, adequacy, distribution, or corrective actions."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e3145b9bc0fb56a3","start_unit":1,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 6 June 2023, the parliamentary speaker said Sheikh Hasina and Sajeeb Wazed Joy had produced unprecedented progress in information technology, that Bangladesh was moving from Digital Bangladesh toward Smart Bangladesh, and that government technology development offered young people a promising future; the event also included budget-analysis and digital-transformation discussions.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.7","6B.2","6B.10","8B.1","8B.2","8B.3","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated 6 June 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The claims are statements by Parliamentary Speaker Shirin Sharmin Chaudhury and describe government policy; they are not independent outcome findings.","limitations":["The extract provides advocacy and event reporting, not audited implementation, budget execution, distributional outcomes, or independent evaluation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-c36204443fd83ece","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"SIPRI's 2023 Bangladesh national budget report page links Bangladesh's 2023-24 demands for grants and appropriations and an operating and development budget resource-use statement.","question_ids":["1B.3","1B.4","2B.8","5B.3","5B.6","8B.2","8B.3"],"polarity":"context","period_fit":"Identified as Bangladesh, year 2023, with 2023-24 budget materials.","ruler_attribution":"The page catalogs national budget documents during Hasina's premiership but does not attribute specific allocations or decisions to her.","limitations":["The supplied extract provides no linked-document contents, amounts, execution data, or assessment of proportionality and effectiveness."]},{"source_id":"SRC-6467f3e8c46407f1","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"In an August 2023 Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha report, Sajeeb Wazed Joy claimed that the 41st BCS examination recommended 2,520 candidates and that the Awami League-led government under Sheikh Hasina had ensured transparency and accountability in public-service recruitment, contrasting it with alleged bribery and political-allegiance-based appointments during the 2001-2006 BNP-Jamaat period.","question_ids":["4B.5","5B.2","5B.5","5B.7","7B.5","7B.8","7B.9","8B.2","8B.4","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Directly dated 8 August 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The favorable claims are made by Hasina's ICT affairs adviser and son, not independently verified in the supplied report.","limitations":["The extract supplies an official-aligned claim and one recruitment result but no independent audit, comparative recruitment data, or evidence about actual implementation and favoritism."]},{"source_id":"SRC-b7ce7ddb0851409a","start_unit":3,"end_unit":4,"fact_summary":"OMCT published the Odhikar Annual Human Rights Report 2023 on 4 January 2024 and described it as covering summary executions, extrajudicial killings, threats, intimidation, harassment, and human-rights defenders; the page also linked contemporaneous calls concerning human rights and democracy before elections and the detention of two defenders.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.8","4B.3","4B.9","7B.6","7B.7","8B.6","8B.9"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"The report concerns 2023 and was published shortly after the period ended.","ruler_attribution":"The extract concerns Bangladesh authorities during Hasina's premiership but does not establish her personal direction or responsibility for each reported incident.","limitations":["Only the OMCT landing-page summary and linked-resource descriptions are supplied; the report's detailed facts, methodology, and findings are unavailable here."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1cb77e1076ef51c7","start_unit":2,"end_unit":2,"fact_summary":"On 26 January 2023, Foreign Minister A.K. Abdul Momen said Bangladesh would accept no more Rohingya arrivals, that Rohingya should return to Myanmar, and that repatriation was Bangladesh's priority; he said more than 1.2 million forcibly displaced Rohingya had been hosted since 2017 and that Myanmar had not repatriated any Rohingya in roughly five and a half years.","question_ids":["2B.1","2B.7","3B.7","6B.3","6B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Directly dated 26 January 2023.","ruler_attribution":"The statements are attributed to the foreign minister, reflecting the government's stated policy; the extract does not show Hasina's personal words or decisions.","limitations":["The report does not assess conditions, voluntariness, safety, or feasibility of repatriation, nor the government's humanitarian implementation."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-c1ddec6b920b6eee","SRC-adea33b1675281f9","SRC-8a5dd8272219d585"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied Amnesty page contains navigation and metadata but no substantive Bangladesh report text.","The supplied digital-security-act study contains only a redirect block, so no findings are available.","The supplied US State Department custom-report page contains only a technical-difficulties message and no report content.","Several sources provide claims or catalog metadata rather than independently verified, ruler-specific evidence; personal attribution to Sheikh Hasina is therefore limited."]}
